scope: Theorem 8.1 (Mixed passage packets) of the manuscript “Uniform bounds for planar polynomial limit cycles” (preprints/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 143 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8ff8e55372a94e4f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 99. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose that the primary inputs are affine combinations of flag scales with constant coefficients and bounded analytic parts, and that all large basis nodes in those combinations have dependent logarithms. For an unbalanced limit, put P = max(L, W) and R = min(L, W) on the reference sequence, and include a primary input Caux → ∞ tied there to P/R. Assume the saturated flag and controlled tests of Sections 2 and 4. Then the outputs of Equations (8.1) and (8.2) satisfy the primitive hypotheses of Assumption 4.2, including fixed independent derivatives, simultaneous safe columns, and refinement invariance of terminal analytic germs. They are retestable for elimination in the sense of Definition 5.6. The amplitude and input smallness is independent of expansion depth. For a family of positive limiting slopes it can also be chosen independently of the slope, provided the ordinary boxes and field bounds are common and every field monomial contains a designated layer whose limiting rate has a common positive lower bound. The other rates need only be positive at each particular limiting slope. Constants and starting points for a fixed packet label may depend on that slope. The two unbalanced cases have common smallness for each fixed rate list.
